mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where both teams hold below-competition-average possession (competition mean ~50%), then examine whether the team with higher shot volume relative to its possession share generates corners at a rate above what its raw possession alone would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kick production rises with shot volume even when possession is suppressed, and the relationship between shots and corners is steeper for the lower-possession side than for higher-possession sides.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When a low-possession team (Team A, ~42% possession) faces an opponent that also operates with low possession (~39%), the combined possession-deficit context suppresses corner kick production for both sides relative to the competition norm, but the team that generates more shots despite low possession (Team A: ~11.7 shots FOR vs Team B: ~10.8 shots FOR) may disproportionately convert shot volume into corners. The joint relationship between a team's own possession share and its shot volume in determining corner kick output is the mechanism to test.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession AND shots) for the same team, not a single observable against one coarse band. It tests a non-linear interaction between possession share and shot volume in producing corners, which is not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the defending team (Team B role) simultaneously allows above-competition-average shots AND holds below-competition-average possession, then measure corner kicks allowed in those matches versus matches where only one condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kicks allowed are elevated when both high shots-against and low possession co-occur, with the joint condition producing a higher corner rate than either condition alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B concedes a structurally high volume of shots (ALL_PRIOR ~16.9, RECENT_5 ~17.4) while also holding low possession (~39.5%). The joint condition of high shots-against AND low possession-for defines a defensive posture where the opponent (Team A) is likely to generate corners at an elevated rate. Test whether the combination of opponent high shots-against rate and own low possession jointly predicts elevated corner kicks allowed, beyond what either variable alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine two-observable joint conditioning (shots-against AND possession-for) on the same team, not a single observable with one coarse band. The interaction between these two dimensions is the novel structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where a team's red card rate exceeds the competition average AND the team concedes above-average shot volumes. Within those matches, compare the ratio of second-half cards to full-match yellow cards against the baseline ratio in matches where only one condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second-half card rate rises disproportionately (relative to full-match yellow cards) when both elevated red card propensity and high shots-against co-occur, indicating a non-additive escalation in the second half.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B carries a notably elevated red card rate (ALL_PRIOR ~0.375 per match, away ~0.5) relative to the competition norm (~0.137). When a team with a high red card rate also concedes high shot volumes (Team B: ~16.9 shots against), test whether the co-occurrence of elevated red card propensity and high shots-against is associated with a disproportionate increase in second-half cards (cards_2h) relative to full-match yellow cards, suggesting a within-match escalation pattern driven by the joint pressure of numerical disadvantage risk and shot volume.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct observables (red card rate AND shots-against) and examines a within-match temporal asymmetry (second-half cards vs full-match cards), combining a two-observable joint condition with a half-level split. Neither element alone is covered.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on match-ups where Team A's cards_2h FOR exceeds its cards_2h AGAINST, AND Team B's cards_2h AGAINST exceeds its cards_2h FOR (i.e., both asymmetries align to inflate second-half cards). Within those match-ups, also examine whether foul rates (Team A fouls FOR ~10.75, Team B fouls AGAINST ~12.96) reinforce the card escalation pattern.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total second-half cards are elevated when both teams' individual second-half card asymmetries (FOR vs AGAINST) point toward higher card production, and this joint alignment produces a higher second-half card total than either team's individual rate alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A generates more second-half cards (FOR: 1.375) than it concedes (AGAINST: 0.875) in the second half, while Team B concedes more second-half cards (AGAINST: 1.625) than it produces (FOR: 1.125). Test whether the asymmetry between a team's own second-half card production and its opponent's second-half card allowance — when both point in the same direction — jointly predicts an elevated total second-half card count, beyond what each team's individual card rate would suggest in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team relationship: it jointly uses Team A's FOR/AGAINST second-half card asymmetry AND Team B's FOR/AGAINST second-half card asymmetry as two distinct dimensions, then adds fouls as a third observable. This is not reducible to a single observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on match-ups where one team improves defensively in the second half (lower goals-against in 2H vs 1H) while the opponent improves offensively in the second half (higher goals-for in 2H vs 1H). Examine whether the net within-match goal distribution (1H vs 2H total goals) is systematically shifted relative to competition baseline, and whether shots_on_target half-level splits reinforce or contradict the goal-timing pattern.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's second-half defensive improvement and the opponent's second-half offensive improvement co-occur, the within-match goal distribution shifts toward the second half, and this shift is amplified relative to what either team's individual half-level goal rate alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A scores more goals in the second half (FOR 2H: 0.583) than the first half (FOR 1H: 0.583 — equal), while conceding more in the first half (AGAINST 1H: 0.875) than the second half (AGAINST 2H: 0.75). Team B scores more in the second half (FOR 2H: 0.708) than the first half (FOR 1H: 0.542), and concedes more in the first half (AGAINST 1H: 0.5) than the second half (AGAINST 2H: 0.792 — reversed). Test whether the joint half-level goal-scoring and goal-conceding profiles of both teams — specifically the interaction between Team A's defensive improvement in the second half and Team B's offensive improvement in the second half — predicts a distinctive within-match goal-timing pattern (more goals in one half than the other) that differs from what each team's individual half-level rates would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on two distinct half-level observables (goals FOR by half AND goals AGAINST by half) for both teams simultaneously, testing a cross-team interaction across two within-match periods. It is not reducible to a single observable's recent vs long-run level, a single half-level split, or a single-band conditioning.
